requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every uncovered item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
I found no gap. Each obligation has code reachable from an `{impl}` root and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Roots and reachability.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[inspect_repository_with_progress]` carries `{impl}`. It calls `rust_coverage::validate_rust_functions`, which calls `rust_files`, `unreferenced_items`, `item_kind`, `EvidenceReads::covers` and `uncovered_error`. All of these are therefore reachable. `src/authoring/coverage_loss.rs#fn[lost_items]` reuses the same `unreferenced_items` and `covers` logic.

**Obligations, code and tests**
- **Parse every first-party `.rs` file among the discovered sources, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory.** `rust_files` filters on the `rs` extension and `!starts_with(root/vendor)`.
  - `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` shows that `src/vendor` and `src/book` files are still checked.
  - `disallowed_paths_are_skipped_and_projects_outside_git_scan_every_file` shows that `vendor/dep/lib.rs` is not covered-checked.
  - `untracked_sources_are_not_validated_until_staged_and_status_lists_them` covers discovery.
- **Cover every function, method (including trait methods and test helpers), struct, enum and union.** `item_kind` maps `fn`, `struct`, `enum` and `union`.
  - `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, test helpers and nested functions.
  - `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside` covers structs, enums and unions.
- **An item is covered by a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}` or `{test}` reference, or a `habeas:util` citation, in an attached comment or inside its body.** `unreferenced_items` scans `outline.comments` by owner (outline comment ownership) and also scans fenced comment citations. Its `counts` closure rejects unknown names, `Term` and `Fixme` references, and built-ins used in a role they don't permit. It also rejects fences that were never closed.
  - `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` covers unknown names, body comments, inner docs, outer docs and trailing comments.
  - `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated`, `habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review` and `a_fixme_does_not_count_as_an_items_reference` cover util, fenced forms, wrong roles and fixme.
- **Evidence coverage.** An item is covered when its node, or a containing node, is recorded with its current hash by an evidence record, citation review or site review. `EvidenceReads::load` reads all evidence files, and `covers` walks up through `node.parent` comparing selector and structural hash.
  - `items_an_assessment_read_with_their_current_hash_are_covered` covers ordinary, citation-review and site-review records, a containing impl block, and a stale hash.
  - `status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form` and the coverage-loss CLI test exercise it end to end.
- **A named example must reference a requirement.** `counts` uses `example_references_requirement`. `an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement` tests tested, orphan, chained and term cases.
- **A string literal, an enclosing module or impl block, or only an evidence input must not count.** Comment ownership uses the outline comment runs, so strings are not comments. `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` tests string and enclosing references, and `comment_scan_skips_string_and_character_literals` exists as well.
- **Report each uncovered item with file, line, kind and name.** `uncovered_error` formats `file:line: kind name is uncovered…`, using `node.declaration_line`. Many tests assert these strings, including `locates_functions_after_unicode_text`, which asserts the line number.
- **Report a Rust parse failure instead of skipping the file.** `validate_rust_functions` pushes `file:line: cannot parse Rust source`. This is asserted in `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` and in `discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference`.

**Unspecified behavior.** I found none. The extra outputs are the progress reporting and the unreadable-source error. Progress reporting is under a separate `{impl}` of `requirements.authoring.progress`, and the unreadable-source error is covered by "report a parse failure instead of skipping".

**Note.** The `{impl}` on the `#[cfg(test)]` helper `missing_function_references` is odd, but it is not a gap under the rules.

text: :::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every uncovered item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} discovery
Habeas MUST find the references of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
in project source files, where {cite}`requirements.references.reference_contexts`
says they count, and MUST fail with the source file and line if a
name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped
roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST
consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in
the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in
both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git`
and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and
generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.
:::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
:::{req} text_search
The harness MUST expose a `ripgrep` tool with this interface:
```text
ripgrep({ pattern: String, path: String = ".", context: Integer = 2,
referencing: Optional<ReferenceScope> }) -> SearchResult
ReferenceScope {
selection: String,                     // full name or definition glob
roles: Array<Role> = ["impl", "test", "cite"],
scope: "node" | "file" = "file",
SearchResult { matches: Array<SearchMatch> }
SearchMatch {
file: String,
item: String,        // selector of the innermost outline node
kind: String,
lines: Array<{ text: String, matched: Boolean }>,
The tool MUST search the requested permitted file or directory using
ripgrep's regular-expression syntax and default case-sensitive search and ignore
rules. It MUST search in process using ripgrep's library crates, without
requiring an external `rg` executable, and MUST apply source-access policy while
walking files rather than filtering results afterwards. It MAY search files in
parallel; results MUST be ordered by path and then line regardless of
parallelism, so the same sources always produce the same inputs. Explicitly allowed paths and discovered generated-output directories MUST
be searched even when ignored or hidden; workspace disallow rules still apply.
`context`
MUST be nonnegative and specify how many lines before and after each matching
line to include, defaulting to two on each side. Windows MUST stop at file
boundaries, and overlapping windows in the same file MUST be merged. The result
MUST give one entry for each innermost outline node containing a match, where a
match in a comment belongs to the node the comment belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`: the node's file, selector
under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, kind, and its matching
and context lines in source order, each marked as matching or not and redacted
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. Results MUST NOT give line
numbers; the model locates and cites code by selector. Separate windows within
one node MUST be distinguishable, such as by an elision line that is not
marked as matching. Search results MUST NOT become
evidence inputs and MUST NOT include definitions; the model-facing description
MUST tell the model to read with the `habeas` tool any node whose code its
conclusion relies on. Setting `context` to zero MUST return only matching lines.
With `referencing`, the tool MUST search only sources, within `path`, that carry
a reference in one of `roles` to a requirement or example the `selection`
matches under {cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`, including
anchors under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: with `scope` `node`, only
the outline nodes that contain or are named by those references, and with
`file`, their whole files. A selection matching no requirement or example, or an
unknown role or scope, MUST return an explanatory tool error. Its model-facing
description MUST explain `referencing`.
Search results MUST exclude files disallowed by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; explicitly requesting an excluded
path MUST be handled as a denial under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
No matches MUST return an empty array; invalid arguments or a failed search MUST
return an explanatory tool error.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
